Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1485
Claimant:
Eric Garcia
Adjuster:
Jerry Hanson
12-3-24
Claim opened after the insured reported a rear-end collision in a parking lot involving the vehicle named on the policy.
The claimant reported knee pain and said she was seated in the other vehicle at the time of impact.
12-30-24
Spoke with the claimant by phone to take her statement. She described the impcat the same way she did during initial
intake and said she had been stopped with her foot on the brake.
1-9-25
Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the damage observed
by the responding officer. No independent witnesses to the impact itself were identified.
1-21-25
Reviewed photos submitted by both parties. They confirm the general position of the vehicles and the location of the
damage, though some details cannot be verified from the images alone.
2-14-25
Inspected the vehicle damage. The pattern and height of the damage match the impact described in the statement
and the police report. A few old scratches near the bumper may predate this collision and were noted separately.
2-21-25
Confirmed coverage was in force at the time of loss and found nothing suggesting the damage occurred before the
policy started. The driver is listed on the policy as a named insured.
3-26-25
Received medical records. The knee injury is consistent in kind and force with the mechanism of this collision.
Records also show a minor strain to the same area many years ago that healed fully without ongoing complaints.
3-31-25
Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits tapering as the claimant's range of
motion and pain improved. The provider's notes describe steady progress with no new complaints recorded in later
visits.
5-6-25
Reviewed the file as a whole. The claimant's account has remained consistent across all contacts, and the
documented injury and vehicle damage align with the reported impact. Moving the claim to the evaluation stage.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
